name: 7z
description: p7zip's archiver: high AES-256 compression/encryption, supports dozens of formats including its own .7z.

flags.description: Extract flat (all files into current dir — usually not what you want).
Encrypt also the file NAMES (header encryption).

examples.explanation: Creates project.7z encrypted with AES-256 (prompts for the password).
Encrypts both contents AND filenames — with plain -p, filenames stay readable.
Lists contents; with header encryption it asks for the password first.

about: 7z offers the strongest widely-available archive encryption (AES-256 + optional header encryption) and good compression. p7zip is the Linux port; the full 7-Zip (7zz, from the 7-Zip project) is newer and faster. For scripts, prefer passing the password via a file or environment rather than -p on the command line.
mistakes: Using -pSECRET on the command line — the password lands in shell history; use the interactive prompt or --password-file where supported.
Using e instead of x and flattening the directory structure.
warnings: If you lose the password, the data is unrecoverable — AES-256 is not brute-forceable in practice.
